title: Using Authentication Service with Zscaler Client Connector Device Tokens

blocks.text: Authentication Service can authenticate users on Zscaler Client Connector using device tokens. With this feature, users need not be tied to your organization’s standard IdP to authenticate to Zscaler Client Connector. Instead, if your organization uses SAML-based single sign-on (SSO), Authentication Service can use a device token to auto-provision and silently authenticate users and devices to Zscaler Client Connector.
To configure Authentication Service to authenticate users on Zscaler Client Connector using device tokens:

blocks.item: 1. Generate device token in Zscaler Client Connector.
2. Enable the device token in Authentication Service.
The user is created in Authentication Service when JIT provisioning is enabled. This user must be assigned the service entitlement to ensure that the login is successful.

The format for the user is <name-of-machine>@<domain> as defined during installation. For example, if the machine name is "Alice" and the domain used at the time of installation is "example.com", the format for the user created is alice@example.com.
Alternatively, you can use the Dynamic Group Registered Domains, a dynamic group, to assign service entitlement. This avoids the need to assign entitlement to individual users.
The Dynamic Group Registered Domains group includes all the users with the domains that are registered to this tenant. Hence, all users in the group are assigned service entitlement automatically.
4. Pass the device token, user domain, and cloud name to users' devices.

To use Authentication Service as an IdP for your users, you must pass the device token generated and copied from Zscaler Client Connector, user domain, and cloud name to users' devices during installation.
For Windows with MSI Installer, see Customizing Zscaler Client Connector with Install Options for MSI.
For Windows with EXE Installer, see Customizing Zscaler Client Connector with Install Options for EXE.
For macOS with Installer App, see Customizing Zscaler Client Connector with Install Options for macOS.
For Android with MDM Deployment procedures, see Customizing Zscaler Client Connector with Install Options for Android.
For iOS with MDM Deployment procedures, see Customizing Zscaler Client Connector with Install Options for iOS.
